about: Newcomers (Docs/Design/52-newcomers.md). The three start towns in order (the first wins a tie), each with a line for the creator and, optionally, an arrival cell and tile; how long an account stays a newcomer; how often active wolves are counted in each town and over how many counts the mean is taken; who may mentor (social level, and no upheld report within so many days); a newcomer's first evenings at an inn (the hours, how many evenings it is tried, how many wolves are pointed out, how well known a regular is); vouching (the bond a voucher needs with the resident, how little it may distrust the one vouched for, the share of trust and liking carried and the most, familiarity given, vouches a voucher may hold, how many game days one lasts, the household's share, and the hit if it goes bad).

starts.name: Ridgemere
starts.line: A rain city on its terraced hills above the Sound: the wharf and the works below, the Sump and the Commons, the Heights at the top, and it always rains.

starts.name: Larkfield
starts.line: A walled market town among the rolling hills and open fields of the Larkdowns, where the south comes to trade.

starts.name: Oakhaven
starts.line: A walled town deep in the Warmwood, the warm broadleaf forest of the south-west, under oaks older than its wall.
